section_summary: This section finishes a November 1948 despatch from London compiling British parliamentary statements on Japan’s economic recovery, trade and demilitarisation, alongside questions about China, Korea, the Philippines and Malaya. It then begins an attached House of Lords debate on the emergency in Malaya, including criticism of British policy and a government account of the insurgency, economic conditions and constitutional plans.

subfiles.title: British parliamentary questions and debates on Far Eastern affairs
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, for the Ambassador, London
subfiles.about: Reports British parliamentary discussion of Japan’s economy and trade and related developments across East and Southeast Asia.
subfiles.summary: The surviving portion opens with debate over Japanese textile expansion, industrial targets, British competition and a Commonwealth trade arrangement. It then records parliamentary answers on Japanese demilitarisation, most-favoured-nation treatment, compensation and trade consultation, followed by exchanges concerning China, Hong Kong, Korea, the Philippines and Malaya. The despatch closes by noting an attached House of Lords debate on Malaya and reporting answers on Malayan arms and rubber exports.

subfiles.title: House of Lords debate: Malaya, 10 November 1948
subfiles.about: Records Lord Mancroft’s criticism and the Earl of Listowel’s response concerning the Malayan Emergency.
subfiles.summary: Lord Mancroft attributes the emergency partly to British administrative and security failures and asks about relations between Chinese and Malay communities, constitutional reform and the future of Singapore. The Earl of Listowel describes the insurgency’s wartime origins, Communist influence in trade unions, armed attacks and the government’s military response. He also discusses production, education, housing, the proposed University of Malaya and plans for elected legislatures. The debate continues beyond page 508.
